name: ʾālep
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters; Driver list via Woudhuizen 2006; WP-Hist acrophony table
notes: Egyptian prototype is the ox-head hieroglyph (WP-Ph table).

name: bēt
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters; Driver list via Woudhuizen 2006; WP-Hist acrophony table
notes: From Egyptian house-plan hieroglyph; Semitic bayt 'house' (WP-Ph).

name: gīmel
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters [ref 22]; Driver list via Woudhuizen 2006; WP-Hist acrophony table
notes: Pictograph-first scholarship reads a thrown hunting club; 'camel' rests on the later letter name (gīmel ~ gamal 'camel').

name: dālet
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters [ref 22]; WP-Hist acrophony table
notes: Scoping §1.2 exemplar row: neither gloss is a prime or an organ of one; alternates are not links.

name: hē
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters; WP-Hist acrophony table; Driver list via Woudhuizen 2006
alternate_glosses: jubilation (haw/hillul) — figure with raised arms; 'lo!, behold' (heʾ)
notes: Origin table glosses the letter 'window'; the Proto-Sinaitic pictograph is a man with upraised arms, acrophonically haw/hillul 'jubilation'.

name: wāw
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters; WP-Hist acrophony table
notes: Driver's list renders the same word 'peg' (Woudhuizen 2006) — a translation variant of one object, not a rival gloss.

name: zayin
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters; WP-Hist (Colless renaming list; Yadin battle-equipment thesis)
notes: Colless: original pictograph name ziqq 'manacle' was replaced by zayin 'weapon'. Draft alternate 'axe' not confirmed in scholarly sources consulted. Weapon-to-DIE link judged too loose under §1.3 rule 4; recorded, not linked.

name: ḥēt
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters; WP-Hist acrophony table
notes: Rival renderings name one object family (an enclosure); origin table marks the pictograph identification '(?)'. Uncertainty recorded; flag consensus per the rival-object line (dossier §2).

name: ṭēt
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters; WP-Hist acrophony table
correlate: the cycle — rotation, the closed ring; corpus seat: the cyclic structure behind the C21 Laplacian
notes: Scoping §1.2 exemplar row. A wheel is the mover's instrument, not the prime MOVE. Jeff's reading (Tet as picture of Gurd Law) is on file, T5, per scoping.

name: yōd
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters; WP-Hist acrophony table; Driver list via Woudhuizen 2006
notes: Hand is the organ of TOUCH and the canonical instrument of DO. With kap, crowds TOUCH (expected synonymy case, scoping §4).

name: kāp
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters; Driver list via Woudhuizen 2006
notes: The palm is the touching surface. Hand/palm/head are the BODY-neighbourhood glyphs: all denote body parts, none denotes BODY.

name: lāmd
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters [ref 24]; WP-Hist acrophony table; Driver list via Woudhuizen 2006
notes: Goad-to-MOVE judged too loose under §1.3 rule 4 (instrument for driving animals, not the prime's instrument); recorded, not linked.

name: mēm
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters; WP-Hist acrophony table; Driver list via Woudhuizen 2006
notes: Water is an instance of a thing, not the prime SOMETHING/THING itself; no denotative link.

name: nūn
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters [ref 22]; WP-Hist (acrophony table; Colless renaming list)
notes: Primary follows the transmitted letter name nun 'fish'; the Proto-Sinaitic pictograph derives from the Egyptian snake hieroglyph (nahs 'snake', renamed per Colless).

name: sāmek
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters; WP-Hist acrophony table; WP-Hist on Yadin 1963
notes: Name samek is from the root s-m-k 'to support'; origin table gives 'pillar(?)' and marks the pictograph disputed; Yadin argued the form depicts battle equipment.

name: ʿayin
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters; WP-Hist acrophony table; Driver list via Woudhuizen 2006
notes: Scoping §1.2 exemplar row: the organ of the prime SEE; the cleanest instrumental link in the set.

name: pē
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters [ref 22]; WP-Hist (acrophony table; Colless renaming list); Driver list via Woudhuizen 2006
notes: Flag CHANGED from scoping draft (consensus): the origin table itself lists 'mouth (or corner)', and Colless records piʾt 'corner' renamed to pe 'mouth'. Link drawn from the primary gloss only: mouth is the organ of SAY.

name: ṣādē
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters; WP-Hist acrophony table
notes: Origin table: 'papyrus plant/fish hook?' — the pictograph identification is unresolved in the sources.

name: qōp
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters; WP-Hist acrophony table
alternate_glosses: cord (of wool), knot (qaw); back of head; needle
notes: Primary CHANGED from scoping draft (cord/knot): the origin table and acrophony list both lead with 'monkey' (qop); priority between monkey and qaw 'cord' is itself disputed and both are recorded.

name: rēš
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters; WP-Hist acrophony table; Driver list via Woudhuizen 2006
notes: Vocalisation variants ros/res are the same word. A body part, not the prime BODY; no link.

name: šīn
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters [ref 22]; WP-Hist (acrophony table; Colless renaming list)
notes: Flag CHANGED from scoping draft (consensus): origin table lists 'tooth (or sun)'; Colless records sims 'sun' renamed to sin 'tooth'; the acrophony table reconstructs sananuma 'bow'. Three rival identifications circulate.

name: tāw
gloss_source: WP-Ph Table of letters; Driver list via Woudhuizen 2006; WP-Hist acrophony table
notes: WP-Hist renders the acrophonic word 'signature' — the same object (a cross-shaped mark), not a rival gloss.
